definition_en: a neat pile of things, to put things in a pile, or the shelves in a library
core_image: 桌上整齐地堆着一摞书
scene: 桌上堆着一摞书。A stack of books lay on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 stack 是「一堆」（第 1 个义项）；句意：桌上堆着一摞书。

senses.title: Neat pile
senses.definition: a neat pile of things placed on top of each other
senses.definitionCN: 一件件叠放整齐的一堆东西
senses.example: A stack of books lay on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上堆着一摞书。
senses.why: This is the central physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最核心的物理义项。

senses.title: Put in a pile
senses.definition: to arrange things in a neat pile
senses.definitionCN: 把东西整齐地叠放起来
senses.example: Please stack the chairs after the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会后请把椅子叠起来。
senses.why: The verb simply names the action.
senses.whyCN: 动词义就是这一动作本身。

senses.title: Library shelves
senses.definition: the shelves or area where books are stored
senses.definitionCN: 存放书籍的书架或区域
senses.example: She found the book in the stacks.
senses.exampleCN: 她在书库里找到了这本书。
senses.why: Library shelves are a long stack of books.
senses.whyCN: 图书馆书架就是一摞摞延伸的书。

intro.en: Stack comes from Old Norse stakkr, a haystack.
intro.cn: stack 来自古诺尔斯语 stakkr，意为草堆。

items.en: Stakkr meant a haystack.
items.cn: stakkr 意为草堆。

items.en: Stack named a pile of hay or wood.
items.cn: stack 指干草或木柴堆。

items.en: The sense widened to any neat pile.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何整齐的堆。

items.en: The verb sense of piling grew later.
items.cn: 「堆叠」的动词义后来出现。

items.en: Library shelves borrowed the word.
items.cn: 图书馆书架借用了这个词。

note.en: Stack is compared with look-alike words and words for piles.
note.cn: 把 stack 与形近词以及表示堆的词作比较。

entries.definition: a pointed post in the ground
things lying on top of each other

normalIntro.en: Stack began as a haystack and now means any neat pile or the act of piling.
normalIntro.cn: stack 原指草堆，如今指任何整齐的堆或堆叠动作。

normal.en: Stack the plates here.
A stack of papers filled the desk.
The chairs stack easily.
Smoke rose from the chimney stack.
He blew his stack at the news.
normal.cn: 听到这个消息他勃然大怒。

abstract.en: Order turns a heap into a stack.
abstract.cn: 秩序把乱堆变成整齐的一摞。

abstract.en: Each layer holds the one above.
abstract.cn: 每一层都托着上面那一层。

abstract.en: A tall pile begins with one item.
abstract.cn: 再高的一摞，也从一件开始。

examples.en: A stack of books lay on the table.
examples.cn: 桌上堆着一摞书。

examples.en: Please stack the chairs after the meeting.
examples.cn: 会后请把椅子叠起来。

examples.en: She found the book in the stacks.
examples.cn: 她在书库里找到了这本书。

dict_mnemonic.text: stack 是「一摞、堆叠」；a stack of books 是一摞书，stack up 是堆积，chimney stack 是烟囱；图书馆的 stacks 指书库。

root: 来自古诺尔斯语 stakkr（草堆），由「干草堆」扩展到任何整齐的堆，再引申出堆叠动作和图书馆书库。

sensesIntro.en: Stack means a neat pile, the act of piling, or library shelves.
sensesIntro.cn: stack 指整齐的一堆、堆叠动作，或图书馆书库。

core.en: Things laid one on top of another.
core.cn: 一件件叠放在彼此之上。

branches.en: Books rise in an even column.
branches.cn: 书本叠成整齐的一列。

branches.en: Hands lift chairs onto one another.
branches.cn: 双手把椅子一把把叠上去。

branches.en: Long shelves fill a quiet room.
branches.cn: 长长的书架填满安静的房间。

branches.en: The pile and the piling share one shape.
branches.cn: 堆好的东西与堆的动作共享同一形态。

branches.en: Shelves are books stacked by design.
branches.cn: 书架就是有意堆叠起来的书。

intro.en: Stack forms verb parts, agent nouns, and compounds.
intro.cn: stack 构成动词变化、施动名词和复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is from Old Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，来自古诺尔斯语。

items.example: A stack of books lay there.

items.meaning: a machine or person that stacks

items.example: The needle is in the haystack.

definition_en: the people who work for an organization, a strong stick, or the five lines of written music
core_image: 职员们拿着文件走过办公室走廊
scene: 全体员工参加了会议。The whole staff attended the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 staff 是「全体职员」（第 1 个义项）；句意：全体员工参加了会议。

senses.title: Employees
senses.definition: all the people who work for an organization
senses.definitionCN: 为一个机构工作的所有人
senses.example: The whole staff attended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 全体员工参加了会议。
senses.why: This is the dominant modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最主要的义项。

senses.title: Walking stick
senses.definition: a long strong stick used for support
senses.definitionCN: 用于支撑身体的长而结实的棍子
senses.example: The old man leaned on his staff.
senses.exampleCN: 老人拄着手杖。
senses.why: This is the oldest concrete sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最具体的义项。

senses.title: Musical lines
senses.definition: the set of five lines on which music is written
senses.definitionCN: 书写音乐用的五条平行线
senses.example: The notes stood on the staff.
senses.exampleCN: 音符写在五线谱上。
senses.why: The five lines look like a bundle of sticks.
senses.whyCN: 五条平行线像一束并排的棍子。

intro.en: Staff comes from Old English stæf, a stick or a letter, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: staff 来自古英语 stæf（棍子、字母），源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant a stick or post.
items.cn: 该词根意为棍子或柱子。

items.en: Stæf meant a stick and also a letter.
items.cn: stæf 既指棍子，也指字母。

items.en: Staff named a rod of support or office.
items.cn: staff 指支撑用的杖或权杖。

items.en: A staff of office came to mean its holders.
items.cn: 权杖的持有者转指全体职员。

items.en: The five musical lines took the name.
items.cn: 音乐的五条线也采用了这个词。

note.en: Staff is compared with look-alike words and words for workers.
note.cn: 把 staff 与形近词以及表示工作人员的词作比较。

entries.definition: the people employed in a place

normalIntro.en: Staff is a supporting stick that grew into a body of workers and a set of music lines.
normalIntro.cn: staff 原是一根支撑的手杖，后来长出「全体职员」和「五线谱」两义。

normal.en: The staff work hard.
We need more staff.
He walked with a staff.
Notes are written on the staff.
The school staff met today.
normal.cn: 学校教职员工今天开了会。

abstract.en: A stick supports one hand; a staff supports a house.
abstract.cn: 一根杖撑住一只手，一群员工撑起一个机构。

abstract.en: Five lines hold a whole song.
abstract.cn: 五条线，托住一整首歌。

abstract.en: What you lean on becomes what you rely on.
abstract.cn: 你所倚靠之物，终成你所依赖之人。

examples.en: The whole staff attended the meeting.
examples.cn: 全体员工参加了会议。

examples.en: The old man leaned on his staff.
examples.cn: 老人拄着手杖。

examples.en: The notes stood on the staff.
examples.cn: 音符写在五线谱上。

dict_mnemonic.text: staff 是「全体职员」，也指「手杖、五线谱」；teaching staff 是教职员工，staff meeting 是员工会议，staff turnover 是员工流动率。

root: 来自古英语 stæf（棍子、字母），源于日耳曼语词根；由「支撑的杖」转指持杖的官员群体，进而指全体职员，五线谱则取其「并排的条」之意。

sensesIntro.en: Staff means employees, a walking stick, or the five lines of music.
sensesIntro.cn: staff 指全体职员、手杖，或音乐的五线谱。

core.en: A strong stick that supports and holds things together.
core.cn: 一根起支撑作用、把事物维系住的结实棍子。

branches.en: Workers fill the office before nine.
branches.cn: 员工在九点前坐满办公室。

branches.en: A hand grips a tall wooden stick.
branches.cn: 一只手握住高高的木杖。

branches.en: Five lines carry a row of notes.
branches.cn: 五条线承载一排音符。

branches.en: The staff of a house supports its work.
branches.cn: 一个机构的员工支撑起它的运转。

branches.en: Office and orchestra both stand on many lines.
branches.cn: 办公室与乐队，都靠许多条线支撑。

intro.en: Staff forms plurals and a small family of work words.
intro.cn: staff 构成复数以及一组与工作相关的词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.exampleCN: 两边的员工在中午会面。
这家诊所人员配备充足。
这里的人员配备是个问题。

definition_en: a raised floor for performing, a period in a process, or to present a play or event
core_image: 灯光亮起，演员走上舞台中央
scene: 演员走上舞台。The actor walked onto the stage.
sceneCN: 这里 stage 是「舞台」（第 1 个义项）；句意：演员走上舞台。

senses.title: Performing platform
senses.definition: a raised floor where actors or musicians perform
senses.definitionCN: 演员或乐手表演用的抬高平台
senses.example: The actor walked onto the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 演员走上舞台。
senses.why: This is the central physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最核心的具体义项。

senses.title: Period of a process
senses.definition: a particular point or period in a process
senses.definitionCN: 过程中的某个时刻或时期
senses.example: The project is at an early stage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目正处于早期阶段。
senses.why: The platform became a step in time.
senses.whyCN: 「台」的概念延伸为时间上的「台阶」。

senses.title: Put on a show
senses.definition: to arrange and perform a play, concert, or event
senses.definitionCN: 安排并演出戏剧、音乐会或活动
senses.example: They staged a new play last night.
senses.exampleCN: 他们昨晚上演了一出新戏。
senses.why: The verb returns to the theatre sense.
senses.whyCN: 动词义又回到戏剧场景。

intro.en: Stage comes from Latin stare, to stand, through Old French estage, a dwelling or floor.
intro.cn: stage 经古法语 estage（住所、楼层）来自拉丁语 stare（站立）。

items.en: Stare meant to stand.
items.cn: stare 意为站立。

items.en: Estage meant a dwelling or a floor.
items.cn: estage 意为住所或楼层。

items.en: Stage named a raised floor or platform.
items.cn: stage 指抬高的地面或平台。

items.en: The theatre sense became dominant.
items.cn: 戏剧舞台义后来占据主导。

items.en: The time sense grew from step by step.
items.cn: 时间义由「一级一级的台阶」引申而来。

note.en: Stage is compared with look-alike words and words for periods.
note.cn: 把 stage 与形近词以及表示阶段的词作比较。

entries.definition: to act or play for people

normalIntro.en: Stage is a raised floor, a step in time, and the act of putting on a show.
normalIntro.cn: stage 是抬高的台、时间中的一步，也是把戏搬上台的动作。

normal.en: She stood on the stage.
The plan is at an early stage.
He has stage fright.
They staged a concert.
normal.cn: 他们举办了一场音乐会。

normal.en: The singer walked to center stage.

abstract.en: Every life has its stages.
abstract.cn: 每个人生都有自己的阶段。

abstract.en: A step up becomes a stage.
abstract.cn: 抬高一步，就成了舞台。

abstract.en: The world watches what you stage.
abstract.cn: 你搬上台的东西，世界都在看。

examples.en: The actor walked onto the stage.
examples.cn: 演员走上舞台。

examples.en: The project is at an early stage.
examples.cn: 这个项目正处于早期阶段。

examples.en: They staged a new play last night.
examples.cn: 他们昨晚上演了一出新戏。

dict_mnemonic.text: stage 是「舞台、阶段、上演」；on stage 是在台上，stage fright 是怯场，early stage 是早期阶段；过去式加 d 变 staged。

root: 经古法语 estage（住所、楼层）来自拉丁语 stare（站立）；由「抬高的台」引申为舞台，再引申为时间中的一个阶段和上演动作。

sensesIntro.en: Stage means a performing platform, a period in a process, or to put on a show.
sensesIntro.cn: stage 指表演的舞台、过程中的阶段，或上演一出戏。

core.en: A raised place where something is shown.
core.cn: 一个被抬高、用来展示某物的场所。

branches.en: Lights rise on a wooden floor.
branches.cn: 灯光照亮木制台面。

branches.en: A chart marks one point in time.
branches.cn: 图表标出时间中的一个节点。

branches.en: Curtains open and the play begins.
branches.cn: 幕布拉开，戏开始了。

branches.en: A platform and a period are both steps.
branches.cn: 台与阶段，都是「一步」。

branches.en: Each staged event moves through stages.
branches.cn: 每场上演的活动都要经过若干阶段。

intro.en: Stage forms verb parts, adjectives, and theatre compounds.
intro.cn: stage 构成动词变化、形容词和戏剧复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is stare, to stand.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 stare，意为站立。

items.meaning: the act of putting on a show

items.exampleCN: 他的声音听起来很做作。
一名舞台工作人员搬动了椅子。

definition_en: a dirty mark, to colour something, or to damage a reputation
core_image: 桌布上一块深色的墨水渍
scene: 墨水在桌布上留下污渍。The ink left a stain on the cloth.
sceneCN: 这里 stain 是「污渍」（第 1 个义项）；句意：墨水在桌布上留下污渍。

senses.title: Dirty mark
senses.definition: a dirty mark that is hard to remove
senses.definitionCN: 难以去除的脏痕
senses.example: The ink left a stain on the cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 墨水在桌布上留下污渍。
senses.why: This is the everyday physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常最常用的具体义项。

senses.title: Colour wood or cloth
senses.definition: to give colour to wood or fabric
senses.definitionCN: 给木材或织物上色
senses.example: They stained the wood dark brown.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把木头染成深棕色。
senses.why: A stain can be wanted, not just dirt.
senses.whyCN: 染色可以是有意为之，而不只是脏污。

senses.title: Damage a name
senses.definition: to damage someone's reputation
senses.definitionCN: 损害某人的名声
senses.example: The scandal stained his name.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩丑闻玷污了他的名声。
senses.why: A mark on cloth became a mark on character.
senses.whyCN: 布上的印记变成了人格上的污点。

intro.en: Stain comes from Old French desteindre, to take colour away, from Latin tingere, to dye.
intro.cn: stain 来自古法语 desteindre（使褪色），源头是拉丁语 tingere（染色）。

items.en: Tingere meant to dye or wet.
items.cn: tingere 意为染色或浸湿。

items.en: Desteindre meant to take colour away.
items.cn: desteindre 意为使褪色。

items.en: Stain meant to discolour or spot.
items.cn: stain 意为使变色、留下斑点。

items.en: The noun named the mark itself.
items.cn: 名词义指印记本身。

items.en: The moral sense grew from visible marks.
items.cn: 道德义由可见的印记引申而来。

note.en: Stain is compared with look-alike words and words for marks.
note.cn: 把 stain 与形近词以及表示印记的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Stain is a mark left behind, whether on cloth, wood, or a name.
normalIntro.cn: stain 是留下的印记，无论在布上、木上，还是在名声上。

normal.en: There is a stain on your shirt.
Use soap on the stain.
They stained the floor brown.
The window has stained glass.
The lie stained his reputation.

abstract.en: Some marks wash out; some do not.
abstract.cn: 有些印记洗得掉，有些洗不掉。

abstract.en: Colour and dirt share one word.
abstract.cn: 色彩与污垢，共用一个词。

abstract.en: A name, once stained, keeps the shape of the mark.
abstract.cn: 名声一旦被玷污，就留下印记的形状。

examples.en: The ink left a stain on the cloth.
examples.cn: 墨水在桌布上留下污渍。

examples.en: They stained the wood dark brown.
examples.cn: 他们把木头染成深棕色。

examples.en: The scandal stained his name.
examples.cn: 这桩丑闻玷污了他的名声。

dict_mnemonic.text: stain 是「污渍」，也指「染色、玷污」；coffee stain 是咖啡渍，stain remover 是去污剂，stained glass 是彩色玻璃；stainless 是不锈的。

root: 来自古法语 desteindre（使褪色），源头是拉丁语 tingere（染色）；由「使布变色」引申为污渍、有意染色，再引申为玷污名声。

sensesIntro.en: Stain means a dirty mark, the act of colouring, or damage to a reputation.
sensesIntro.cn: stain 指污渍、染色，或对名声的玷污。

core.en: A colour mark left on a surface.
core.cn: 留在表面上的颜色印记。

branches.en: Ink spreads into a dark patch.
branches.cn: 墨水晕开成一块深色印记。

branches.en: A brush lays colour on wood.
branches.cn: 刷子把颜色涂在木头上。

branches.en: Whispers leave a shadow on a name.
branches.cn: 流言在名声上留下阴影。

branches.en: The same mark may be dirt or design.
branches.cn: 同一个印记，可能是污垢，也可能是设计。

branches.en: Cloth and character both keep a mark.
branches.cn: 布匹与人格，都会留下印记。

intro.en: Stain forms verb parts and a family of colour words.
intro.cn: stain 构成动词变化以及一组与颜色相关的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is tingere, to dye.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁语源头是 tingere，意为染色。

items.example: The stain will not come out.
There are stains on the rug.
Staining the table takes a day.

items.exampleCN: 两名染色工在那里干活。

definition_en: a set of steps inside a building, or one single step
core_image: 老宅里一段木制楼梯向上延伸
scene: 她慢慢走上楼梯。She walked slowly up the stairs.
sceneCN: 这里 stair 是「楼梯」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她慢慢走上楼梯。

senses.title: Flight of steps
senses.definition: a set of steps that leads from one floor to another
senses.definitionCN: 连接上下楼层的一组台阶
senses.example: She walked slowly up the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她慢慢走上楼梯。
senses.why: The plural form is the usual word for the whole flight.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式通常指整段楼梯。

senses.title: Single step
senses.definition: one step in a set of stairs
senses.definitionCN: 一组楼梯中的一级台阶
senses.example: He sat on the bottom stair.
senses.exampleCN: 他坐在最下面一级台阶上。
senses.why: The singular names just one step.
senses.whyCN: 单数形式只指一级台阶。

intro.en: Stair comes from Old English stæger, a set of steps, from a Germanic root meaning to climb.
intro.cn: stair 来自古英语 stæger（一组台阶），源于意为「攀爬」的日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant to climb or rise.
items.cn: 该词根意为攀爬、上升。

items.en: Stæger meant a set of steps.
items.cn: stæger 意为一组台阶。

items.en: Stair named one step of a flight.
items.cn: stair 指一段楼梯中的一级。

items.en: The plural stairs became the usual name for a flight.
items.cn: 复数 stairs 成为整段楼梯的常用说法。

items.en: Compounds like staircase and stairway grew from it.
items.cn: staircase、stairway 等复合词由此产生。

note.en: Stair is compared with look-alike words and words for steps.
note.cn: 把 stair 与形近词以及表示台阶的词作比较。

entries.definition: a flat surface for the foot
a set of stairs and its frame
a frame with rungs for climbing

normalIntro.en: Stair is one step in the singular and the whole flight in the plural.
normalIntro.cn: stair 单数是一级台阶，复数则指整段楼梯。

normal.en: Go up the stairs.
The stairs are steep.
She sat on the bottom stair.
normal.cn: 她坐在最下面一级台阶上。

normal.en: He fell down the stairs.
They carried the box upstairs.

abstract.en: Every climb is made of single steps.

core.en: A step that carries you upward.

branches.en: The whole stair reaches the upper room.

intro.en: Stair forms plurals and compounds for parts of a building.

definition_en: a strong post in the ground, a share in a business, or something important that may be lost
core_image: 一根木桩被敲进松软的泥土

senses.title: Pointed post

senses.example: He drove the stake into the ground.

senses.title: Share or interest

senses.title: Risk something

senses.why: The noun of a pledge became a verb of risking.

intro.en: Stake comes from Old English staca, a post, from a Germanic root.

items.en: The root meant a post or peg.

to risk money on a result
a part of a company's value

normalIntro.en: Stake is a post in the ground, a claim marked by it, and the risk behind the claim.

normal.en: She staked her savings on the race.

abstract.en: A post marks what a hand claims.

abstract.en: What you own is also what you may lose.

abstract.en: Every claim has a risk tied to it.
abstract.cn: 每一份权利，都系着风险。

examples.en: He drove the stake into the ground.

examples.en: She has a stake in the company.

examples.en: He staked his reputation on the plan.
examples.cn: 他拿自己的声誉押在这个计划上。

dict_mnemonic.text: stake 是「木桩」，也指「股份、利害关系」，动词意为「押上」；at stake 是事关重大，have a stake in 是与……有利害关系。

root: 来自古英语 staca（桩），源于日耳曼语词根；由插桩标界引申为所有权与股份，再引申为拿有价值之物冒险。

sensesIntro.en: Stake means a post, a share or interest, or to risk something valuable.

core.en: A marker driven into the ground.

branches.en: A mallet drives wood into soil.

branches.en: A name sits on a list of owners.

branches.en: Coins are pushed across a table.
branches.cn: 硬币被推过桌面。

branches.cn: 木桩与股份，都在标出权利。

branches.en: To hold a share is to carry a risk.

intro.en: Stake forms verb parts and compounds of claim and watch.

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.

definition_zh: 不新鲜的；陈旧的；走味的
definition_en: no longer fresh, or no longer interesting because it is too familiar
core_image: 一块放久了变硬的面包
scene: 面包放久变硬了。The bread has gone stale.

senses.title: Not fresh
senses.definition: no longer fresh, especially of food

senses.example: The bread has gone stale.

senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.

senses.title: Old and dull
senses.definition: no longer interesting because it is too familiar
senses.definitionCN: 因过于熟悉而不再有趣
senses.example: His jokes are getting stale.
senses.exampleCN: 他的笑话越来越老套。
senses.why: Food going stale became ideas going dull.
senses.whyCN: 食物变味，引申为想法乏味。

senses.title: Without life
senses.definition: flat or lifeless, as of air or a performance

senses.why: Staleness can be felt without taste.

intro.en: Stale comes from Old French estale, fixed or standing, of uncertain deeper origin.

items.en: The deeper origin is not certain.

items.en: Estale meant fixed or settled.
items.cn: estale 意为固定的、停滞的。

items.en: Stale described drink or food gone flat.
items.cn: stale 描述走味的饮料或食物。

items.en: The sense widened to anything old.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何陈旧之物。

items.en: Stale jokes and stale air both became common.
items.cn: 「老掉牙的笑话」和「污浊的空气」都成了常见说法。

note.en: Stale is compared with look-alike words and words for old or dry.

entries.definition: having existed for a long time

normalIntro.en: Stale means time has taken the freshness out of food, air, or jokes.
normalIntro.cn: stale 指时间抽走了食物、空气或笑话里的新鲜感。

normal.en: This bread is stale.
Open a window; the air is stale.
The joke felt stale.
Their marriage had gone stale.
normal.cn: 他们的婚姻已失去活力。

normal.en: Stale smoke hung in the room.
normal.cn: 陈腐的烟味滞留在房间里。

abstract.en: Even honey loses its shine in time.

abstract.en: Repetition turns wonder into habit.

abstract.en: Freshness is a guest, not a resident.

examples.en: The bread has gone stale.
examples.cn: 面包放久变硬了。

examples.en: His jokes are getting stale.
examples.cn: 他的笑话越来越老套。

examples.en: The room was full of stale air.

dict_mnemonic.text: stale 是「不新鲜的、陈旧的」；stale bread 是不新鲜的面包，stale air 是污浊的空气，go stale 是变味、变陈旧。

root: 来自古法语 estale（固定不动的），更早来源不确定；由「停滞不动」引申为食物走味、空气沉闷、想法陈旧。

sensesIntro.en: Stale means no longer fresh, old and dull, or flat and lifeless.
sensesIntro.cn: stale 指不再新鲜、陈旧乏味，或沉闷无生气。

core.en: Freshness lost through time.

branches.en: A loaf hardens on the shelf.
branches.cn: 面包在架子上变硬。

branches.en: A familiar joke draws no laugh.
branches.cn: 熟悉的笑话引不来笑声。

branches.en: Closed windows keep the room heavy.

branches.en: Food and humour both lose their edge.
branches.cn: 食物与幽默，都会失去锋芒。

branches.en: What is repeated becomes airless.
branches.cn: 被重复的东西，会变得不透气。

intro.en: Stale forms comparisons, an adverb, and a noun.

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word came through Old French.

items.example: The staleness of the air was clear.

definition_en: a small open shop, to stop working suddenly, or to delay
core_image: 市场里摆满水果的木制摊位

senses.title: Market stand

senses.definitionCN: 发动机等突然停止运转

definition_en: a rule or measure used to judge quality, a level of quality, or the usual accepted type

senses.title: Rule for judging

definition_en: a position from which someone views or judges an issue
core_image: 一个人站在原地观察四周
scene: 从她的立场看，这个决定合理。From her standpoint, the decision makes sense.
sceneCN: 这里 standpoint 是「立场」（第 1 个义项）；句意：从她的立场看，这个决定合理。

senses.title: Side taken
senses.definition: the side that a person stands on in a discussion or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 在讨论或争论中一个人所站的一方
senses.example: From her standpoint, the decision makes sense.

senses.why: The physical place of standing is the base image.

senses.title: Opinion held

senses.definitionCN: 对某个问题的特定看法

senses.why: A place to stand became a side to take.

senses.title: Angle of view
senses.definition: the angle from which something is viewed or told

senses.why: A position in space became an angle of view.

senses.title: By statistical methods
senses.definition: in a way that uses statistical methods or rests on summarized numerical evidence
senses.definitionCN: 以使用统计方法或依据汇总数值证据的方式
senses.example: Statistically, the survey is the best evidence we have.
senses.exampleCN: 从统计上看，这次调查是我们手上最好的证据。
senses.why: The adverb -ly turns the adjective into a standpoint: the speaker asks the listener to judge the claim by counting and probability rather than by impression.
senses.whyCN: 副词词尾 -ly 把形容词变成一种立场：说话人要求听者用计数与概率而不是凭印象来判断这一说法。

senses.title: At the threshold of significance
senses.titleCN: 达到统计显著：差距大到不像偶然
senses.definition: used with significant, meaning that the observed difference is large enough relative to random variation to be unlikely by chance
senses.definitionCN: 与 significant 连用，表示观察到的差异相对于随机波动足够大，不太可能出于偶然
senses.example: The new drug lowered blood pressure statistically significantly.
senses.exampleCN: 新药在统计上显著降低了血压。
senses.why: This is the most common use in research writing: the adverb tells the reader that the result passed a pre-set probability test, not that the effect was large in daily life.
senses.whyCN: 这是研究写作中最常见的用法：副词告诉读者结果通过了预设的概率检验，并不表示效果在日常生活中很大。

senses.title: In terms of calculated probability
senses.definition: used to state how likely something is according to probability calculated from data
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明依据数据计算出的概率，某事有多大的可能性
senses.example: Statistically, a passenger is safer in a bus than in a car.
senses.exampleCN: 从统计概率看，乘客坐公交车比坐小汽车更安全。
senses.why: Here the adverb shifts the frame from one journey to many journeys, so that risk is read off a distribution rather than off a single event.
senses.whyCN: 这里副词把视角从一次行程移到许多次行程，于是风险是从分布上读出的，而不是从单一事件读出的。

senses.title: With no detectable difference
senses.definition: used with words such as indistinguishable or equivalent, meaning that the data show no difference large enough to detect
senses.definitionCN: 与 indistinguishable、equivalent 等词连用，表示数据显示不出足够大的差异
senses.example: The two samples were statistically indistinguishable.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个样本在统计上无法区分。
senses.why: Statistically here marks a limit of evidence, not a proof of sameness: the method cannot separate the cases, which is a different claim from saying they are identical.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 statistically 标记证据的极限，而不是证明相同：方法无法把两者分开，这与「它们完全相同」是不同的主张。

senses.title: As a representative sample
senses.definition: used of a sample, meaning that its composition matches the larger population closely enough for inference
senses.definitionCN: 用于样本，表示其构成与更大总体足够接近，可以进行推断
senses.example: The panel was statistically representative of the electorate.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小组在统计上代表了全体选民。
senses.why: Representativeness is a statistical property, not a moral one; the adverb says the sample was checked against known proportions of the population.
senses.whyCN: 代表性是一种统计属性，而不是道德属性；副词说明该样本已对照总体的已知比例作过检验。

senses.title: As a way of framing a claim
senses.titleCN: 从统计角度来说（话语标记）
senses.definition: used as a discourse marker to announce that the following statement is a statistical generalization rather than a personal observation
senses.definitionCN: 作话语标记，提示接下来的陈述是统计概括，而不是个人观察
senses.example: Statistically speaking, most errors happen in the first week.
senses.exampleCN: 从统计角度来说，大多数错误发生在第一周。
senses.why: The phrase softens and frames: it warns the listener that exceptions exist, while asserting that the pattern holds across the counted cases.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语起缓冲与框定作用：它提醒听者存在例外，同时断言这一模式在被计数的案例中成立。

senses.title: On average, in the typical case
senses.titleCN: 按平均值、在典型情况下
senses.definition: in the average case, as opposed to an extreme or atypical one
senses.definitionCN: 在平均值情形下，而不是在极端或非典型情形下
senses.example: Statistically, the average household spends a fifth of its income on housing.
senses.exampleCN: 从统计平均看，普通家庭把五分之一的收入花在住房上。
senses.why: Averages hide variation, and the adverb signals that the statement is about the middle of a distribution, where no single family need actually sit.
senses.whyCN: 平均值会掩盖差异，这个副词提示该陈述针对分布的中间位置，而未必有任何一个家庭真的处在那里。

senses.title: Too small to matter in practice
senses.titleCN: 统计上可忽略：效应小到无实际意义
senses.definition: used of an effect or risk, meaning that it is measurably present but so small that it can be disregarded in practice
senses.definitionCN: 用于效应或风险，表示它在测量上确实存在，但小到在实际中可忽略
senses.example: The added risk was statistically negligible.
senses.exampleCN: 增加的风险在统计上可忽略不计。
senses.why: This sense separates statistical existence from practical importance: a difference can be real in the data and still be too small to act on.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把「统计上存在」与「实际重要」分开：差异在数据中可能真实存在，却仍小到不值得采取行动。

intro.en: Statistically is statistical plus the native adverb ending -ly, whose Old English ancestor -lice marked manner. Statistical itself rests on statistics, a German academic coinage from New Latin statisticum and Latin status.
intro.cn: statistically 是 statistical 加本族副词词尾 -ly，其古英语前身 -lice 标记方式。statistical 又建立在 statistics 之上，后者是德国学界由新拉丁 statisticum 与拉丁 status 构成的造词。

items.en: Latin status 'condition, state' comes from stare 'to stand' and gives the whole family its base.
items.cn: 拉丁 status「状况、国家」出自 stare「站立」，为整个词族提供词基。

items.en: Statistik was fixed in 1749 as the name of the descriptive science of state facts; English statistics followed late in the century.
items.cn: Statistik 在 1749 年被固定为描述国家事实的学问之名；英语 statistics 在该世纪后期跟进。

items.en: The adjective statistical was formed on statistics and later applied to probability and sampling.
items.cn: 形容词 statistical 由 statistics 构成，后来应用于概率与抽样。

items.en: The Old English suffix -lice, later -ly, formed manner adverbs from adjectives; English applied it freely to statistical once the adjective existed.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -lice（后为 -ly）由形容词构成方式副词；statistical 一旦存在，英语便自由地加上这一词尾。

items.en: In the twentieth century statistically fixed its collocations in research writing, above all statistically significant, and later statistically indistinguishable and statistically negligible.
items.cn: 二十世纪，statistically 在研究写作中固定了搭配，最重要的是 statistically significant，后来又出现 statistically indistinguishable 与 statistically negligible。

items.en: The exact first English citation of statistically is uncertain. The deeper root of stare is reconstructed as Indo-European *sta-, a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：statistically 的英语最早书证年代不确定。stare 的更深词根被重构为印欧语 *sta-，属重构形式，并非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: The first group separates the statistics family by part of speech; the second gives near-synonyms for the standpoint the adverb marks.
note.cn: 第一组按词性区分 statistics 词族；第二组给出与该副词所标立场相近的说法。

entries.definition: Describes a noun, such as a method or a result. Statistically describes how a verb is done or how a claim is framed.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰名词，如方法或结果；statistically 描述动作怎样完成或主张如何被框定。

entries.definition: The field or the data. It cannot stand where the adverb stands.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科或数据，不能出现在副词的位置上。

entries.definition: One computed number. The adverb never names a number; it names a way of judging.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个计算出的数值；副词从不命名数字，而是命名判断方式。

entries.definition: The analyst. Statistically refers to the method the analyst uses, not the analyst.
entries.definitionCN: 指分析者；statistically 指分析者所用的方法，而不是分析者本人。

entries.definition: Expressed as figures. It does not say whether the figures were sampled or tested.
entries.definitionCN: 指以数字表达，并不说明这些数字是否经过抽样或检验。

entries.definition: In terms of quantity rather than quality. It is broader and less technical than statistically.
entries.definitionCN: 指从数量而非性质角度，比 statistically 更宽泛、更不技术化。

entries.definition: In terms of probability. A model can be probabilistic without using measured data, so the words are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 指从概率角度；模型可以是概率性的而不使用实测数据，因此两者不能随意互换。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for the middle of a distribution; it matches the 'typical case' sense but not the significance sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指分布中间的日常说法；它对应「典型情况」义项，但不对应显著性义项。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: statistical + -ly: judge the claim by the numbers.
normal.cn: statistical + -ly：用数字来判断这一说法。

normal.en: The family runs statistics, statistic, statistician, statistical, biostatistics.
Fixed phrases carry the sense: statistically significant, statistically indistinguishable, statistically speaking.
normal.cn: 固定搭配承载词义：统计显著、统计上无法区分、从统计角度来说。

normal.en: A result can be statistically real and still too small to matter.
normal.cn: 结果可以在统计上真实存在，却仍小到不重要。

normal.en: Statistically answers 'by what measure?', not 'how much?'
normal.cn: statistically 回答「用什么度量判断」，而不是「有多少」。

abstract.en: Picture two curves lying inside the same error band.
abstract.cn: 想象两条曲线落在同一条误差带里。

abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子，最小的刻度标着「证据不足」。

examples.en: Statistically, the two schools differ by less than one point.
examples.cn: 从统计上看，两所学校的差距不到一分。

examples.en: The treatment worked statistically, though few patients noticed a change.
examples.cn: 该疗法在统计上有效，尽管很少有病人感到变化。

examples.en: Statistically speaking, the risk rises sharply after the age of sixty.
examples.cn: 从统计角度来说，风险在六十岁之后急剧上升。

root: 拉丁 status「国家、状态」（出自 stare「站立」）→ 新拉丁 statisticum → 德语 Statistik → 英语 statistics → statistical + -ly。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses cover the plain standpoint, the significance threshold, calculated odds, undetectable difference, representative sampling, discourse framing, the average case and practical negligibility.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项覆盖：一般统计立场、显著性门槛、计算出的概率、无法检出的差异、代表性抽样、话语框定、平均情形，以及实际可忽略性。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two results sit inside one error band, and the ruler decides whether they differ.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个结果落在同一条误差带里，由标尺决定它们是否不同。

branches.en: THE STANDPOINT: judge by data and method rather than by impression.
branches.cn: 立场：用数据与方法判断，而不是凭印象。

branches.en: THE SIGNIFICANCE LINE: the difference passes a pre-set chance test.
branches.cn: 显著性界线：差异通过了预设的偶然性检验。

branches.en: ODDS AND REPRESENTATION: probability read from a distribution, and a sample that mirrors it.
branches.cn: 概率与代表性：从分布读出的概率，以及与之相称的样本。

branches.en: LIMITS OF EVIDENCE: no detectable difference, and a framing phrase that admits exceptions.
branches.cn: 证据的限度：检不出差异，以及承认例外的框定说法。

branches.en: THE MIDDLE VERSUS THE TRIVIAL: the average case, and an effect too small to act on.
branches.cn: 中间情形与微不足道：平均情形，以及小到无需行动的效应。

intro.en: Statistically is a three-layer English word: statistics from German and New Latin, the adjective ending -al, and the native manner-adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: statistically 是三层构成的英语词：来自德语与新拉丁的 statistics，形容词词尾 -al，以及本族方式副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is status 'state, condition', from stare 'to stand', carried into New Latin statisticum and then into German and English.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的拉丁成分是 status「国家、状况」，出自 stare「站立」，经新拉丁 statisticum 进入德语与英语。

definition_en: the science of collecting and analysing numerical data, or the data so collected
core_image: 一张大表被逐行汇总成几根柱子和一条曲线，边上写着总人数
scene: 年报用大量数字说明过去一年的变化。The statistics show a steady decline in rainfall.
sceneCN: 这里指「汇总起来的统计数据」（第 2 个义项：统计数据）；句意为这些统计数据显示降雨量持续下降。可辨识物件：年报、数据表、柱状图、计算器。

pos.zh: 统计学（作单数）；统计数据（作复数）；统计资料

senses.title: The science of numerical data
senses.definition: the branch of mathematics that collects, summarises and analyses data
senses.definitionCN: 收集、汇总与分析数据的数学分支
senses.example: Statistics is taught as a separate subject in the second year.
senses.exampleCN: 统计学在第二年作为独立科目教授。
senses.why: The discipline takes a plural form but a singular verb, because the name of a field is treated as one subject.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科形式上是复数，动词却用单数，因为学科名称被当作一个整体。

senses.title: Numerical data collected
senses.definition: sets of numbers gathered about a population or an activity
senses.definitionCN: 关于某个群体或某项活动收集起来的一组组数字
senses.example: The statistics show a steady decline in rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这些统计数据显示降雨量持续下降。
senses.why: The same form names the data as well as the study: what the discipline produces is called by its name.
senses.whyCN: 同一形式既指学科也指数据：学科产出的东西就以学科命名。

senses.title: Official published figures
senses.definition: figures regularly published by a government or an agency
senses.definitionCN: 政府或机构定期发布的数字
senses.example: The official statistics are revised every quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 官方统计数据每季度修订一次。
senses.why: Public numbers carry authority, so the word often means the official series rather than any calculation.
senses.whyCN: 公开的数字带有权威，因此这个词常指官方序列，而非任何计算。

senses.title: The use of statistical methods
senses.definition: the application of statistical methods to a question
senses.definitionCN: 把统计方法用到某个问题上
senses.example: The paper's statistics are sound but its sampling is weak.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文的统计处理可靠，取样却较弱。
senses.why: Judging a study means judging how its numbers were handled, and the word covers that handling.
senses.whyCN: 评价一项研究就是评价它的数字如何被处理，这个词覆盖那套处理。

senses.title: A table of summary figures
senses.definition: a table or set of summary figures presented together
senses.definitionCN: 一起呈现的一张汇总表或一组汇总数字
senses.example: The appendix prints the statistics by region.
senses.exampleCN: 附录按地区列出了这些统计数字。
senses.why: Collected numbers are usually presented as a table, and the table itself comes to be called the statistics.
senses.whyCN: 收集来的数字通常以表格呈现，表格本身也就被称作统计数据。

senses.title: Performance figures in sport
senses.definition: recorded numbers describing players' or teams' performance
senses.definitionCN: 记录球员或球队表现的数字
senses.example: His statistics improved sharply after the coaching change.
senses.exampleCN: 换教练之后，他的数据大幅提升。
senses.why: Sport applies the word to any counted record, especially when it is used to judge performance.
senses.whyCN: 体育把这个词用于任何计数记录，尤其当它被用来评判表现时。

senses.title: A single computed value
senses.definition: one computed value such as an average or a rate, in the singular form
senses.definitionCN: 以单数形式出现的一个计算值，如平均值或比率
senses.example: One statistic stands out: the median age has doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 有一个数字很突出：年龄中位数翻了一番。
senses.why: English keeps a singular form for one item and reserves the plural for the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 英语为一个条目保留单数形式，把复数留给整组数据。

senses.title: A way of describing a population by numbers
senses.definition: the practice of describing a whole population through counted features
senses.definitionCN: 通过计数特征来描述整个群体的做法
senses.example: Statistics turns a crowd into a shape one can compare with another crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 统计把一群人变成一个可以与他人比较的形状。
senses.why: The abstract sense names the move from many individuals to one describable profile.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义指从许多个体走向一个可描述轮廓的那一步。

intro.en: Statistics comes from German Statistik, a word coined in the eighteenth century for the systematic description of a state, from New Latin statisticum 'of state affairs' and Latin status 'state, condition'.
intro.cn: statistics 出自德语 Statistik，这个词在十八世纪被造出来，指对一个国家状况的系统描述；再上溯新拉丁 statisticum「国家事务的」与拉丁 status「状态、状况」。

items.en: Status meant 'standing, condition, state'. It comes from stare 'to stand', a verb of long standing in Latin.
items.cn: status 意为「处境、状况、状态」，出自 stare「站立」，这是一个在拉丁语中由来已久的动词。

items.en: The phrase statisticum collegium, a course on state affairs, supplied the adjective from which the German noun was formed.
items.cn: 短语 statisticum collegium 指关于国家事务的课程，提供了构成德语名词的形容词。

items.en: The German noun Statistik was coined in the eighteenth century for the systematic description of a state's resources and people.
items.cn: 德语名词 Statistik 在十八世纪被造出，指对国家资源与人口的系统描述。

items.en: English adopted statistics in the late eighteenth century, at first for the descriptive study of states and only later for numerical methods in general.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪末采用 statistics，最初指对国家的描述性研究，后来才泛指数值方法。

items.en: The plural ending survives from the German and Latin forms, but the discipline is treated as singular while the data remain plural.
items.cn: 复数词尾来自德语与拉丁形式，但这门学科被当作单数，而数据仍作复数。

items.en: The modern sense of analysing variation and probability is a nineteenth-century growth; early dates for particular uses are approximate.
items.cn: 分析变异与概率的现代义是十九世纪的发展；各个具体用法的早期年代只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms and relatives of the same word; group two holds words for the numbers themselves or for the study of them.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的形式与亲属词；第二组是表示数字本身或研究它们的词。

entries.definition: The singular form for a single computed value, not the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 单数形式，指一个计算值，而不是这门学科。

entries.definition: Relating to statistics or to methods of analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 关于统计学或分析方法的形容词。

entries.definition: A person who works with statistics, formed with the personal ending -ian.
entries.definitionCN: 从事统计工作的人，由表示人的词尾构成。

entries.definition: The plural form takes a singular verb for the subject and a plural verb for the data, a classic trap.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式用于学科时接单数动词，用于数据时接复数动词，是常见陷阱。

entries.definition: Collected observations before analysis; statistics is the analysis of such data.
entries.definitionCN: 分析之前的原始观察；统计学就是对这类数据的分析。

entries.definition: Numerical results as printed or quoted, with no claim of method.
entries.definitionCN: 印出或引用的数值结果，不涉及方法。

entries.definition: A set of chosen measures used to judge performance, common in business.
entries.definitionCN: 一组用来评判表现的选定度量，常用于商业。

entries.definition: The mathematics of chance, on which much of statistics rests.
entries.definitionCN: 关于机会的数学，统计学大量依赖它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word began as a description of the state, which is why its oldest relative is the word for condition and standing.
normal.cn: 这个词最初是「对国家状况的描述」，因此它最古老的亲属词是表示「状况、处境」的词。

normal.en: One family runs statistics, statistic, statistical, statistically and statistician.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：统计学、统计量、统计的、从统计上看、统计学家。

normal.en: Remember the number agreement: the subject takes a singular verb, the data take a plural one.
normal.cn: 记住单复数搭配：指学科用单数动词，指数据用复数动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: official statistics, vital statistics, the statistics show.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：官方统计数据、人口动态统计、统计数据显示。

normal.en: A single value is a statistic; the whole set or the science is statistics.
normal.cn: 一个数值是「统计量」，整组数据或这门学问是「统计学」。

abstract.en: Picture a long table of figures shrinking into three bars and one smooth curve.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长长的数字表缩成三根柱子和一条平滑曲线。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd of people replaced by a single outline that can be compared with another crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人被一个轮廓替代，而这个轮廓能与另一群人相比。

abstract.en: Picture a government office printing the same table every quarter, whatever the weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一个政府办公室每季度印出同一张表，无论晴雨。

examples.en: Statistics is compulsory for students in this programme.
examples.cn: 统计学是这个项目的必修课。

examples.en: The statistics were collected over five years.
examples.cn: 这些统计数据是五年间收集的。

examples.en: One statistic surprised the panel: the rate had doubled.
examples.cn: 有一个数字让评审组吃惊：比率翻了一番。

dict_mnemonic.text: 这个词最初指「对国家状况的系统描述」，词根是表示「状态、处境」的拉丁词；后来从描述国家转到描述任何群体的数字，学科与数据都用同一个形式。

root: 德语 Statistik（十八世纪造词，指对国家状况的系统描述）经新拉丁 statisticum「国家事务的」上溯拉丁 status「状态、处境」，status 出自 stare「站立」。英语十八世纪末采用，先指国家描述，后泛指数值分析。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: many separate facts are turned into a few numbers that describe a whole. The movement is then called a science, a set of published figures, a method, a table, a player's record and, at last, a way of seeing a population.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把许多分散的事实变成少数描述整体的数字。这个动作再依次被称为一门学科、一组公布的数字、一种方法、一张表、一名球员的记录，最后成为看一个群体的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table of figures shrinking into a few bars and one curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长长的数字表缩成几根柱子和一条曲线。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE: the discipline collects and analyses numbers by fixed rules.
branches.cn: 学科：这门学问按固定规则收集与分析数字。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: collected data and the table that presents them share the name.
branches.cn: 数字：收集的数据与呈现它们的表格共用同一个名称。

branches.en: PUBLISHED RECORDS: official series and sports records are both counted and quoted.
branches.cn: 公布的记录：官方序列与体育记录都是被计数并被引用的。

branches.en: THE UNIT: methods handle numbers, and one computed value is a statistic.
branches.cn: 单位：方法处理数字，而一个计算值就是一个统计量。

branches.en: THE VIEW: the same move turns a crowd into one profile that can be compared with another.
branches.cn: 眼光：同一个动作把一群人变成一个可以与他人比较的轮廓。

intro.en: Statistics is a German coinage on a Latin base, and the family splits into the science, a single value, the adjective and the person.
intro.cn: statistics 是一个以拉丁语为底、在德语中造出的词；词族分成学科、单个值、形容词与从业者。

latinIntro.en: Latin status 'state, standing' gives statisticum and German Statistik; English adds statistic, statistical and statistician.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 status「状态、处境」给出 statisticum 与德语 Statistik；英语再加 statistic、statistical、statistician。

items.example: The root names the state being described.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被描述的那个状态。

items.example: The New Latin adjective supplied the German noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个新拉丁形容词提供了德语名词。

items.meaning: the science of data; the data

items.exampleCN: 这些组在统计上有差异。

items.meaning: a person who works with statistics
items.exampleCN: 一位统计学家审查了设计。

items.structure: statista (New Latin noun, 'one skilled in state affairs')
items.meaning: a person versed in affairs of state
items.example: The early statisticians were often described as statistas.
items.exampleCN: 早期的统计工作者常被称作熟悉国家事务的人。
